definitions.explanation: A princess or daughter of noble birth. In historical and fairy-tale contexts, refers to the daughter of a lord, emperor, or other high-ranking figure.
When used as a prefix, indicates a smaller or more delicate variety of something, often plants or animals. This usage derives from the association of {姫|ひめ} with femininity and daintiness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姫|ひめ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。

examples.english: This Japanese stewartia has small, delicate flowers.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{姫|ひめ}さま: princess (polite/fairy-tale style)
- お{姫|ひめ}さま{抱|だ}っこ: bridal carry ("princess carry")
- {姫|ひめ}{君|ぎみ}: princess, noble lady (classical/literary)

AS A PREFIX:
{姫|ひめ}〜 indicates a smaller or more delicate version of something:
- {姫|ひめ}リンゴ: crab apple (small apple)
- {姫|ひめ}シャラ: Japanese stewartia (smaller than シャラ)
- {姫|ひめ}{百合|ゆり}: star lily (small lily species)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{姫|ひめ} appears in many famous Japanese stories: かぐや{姫|ひめ} (Princess Kaguya), {乙|おと}{姫|ひめ} (Princess Otohime from Urashima Taro), and many others. In modern usage, it sometimes appears as slang meaning a pampered or princess-like girl.
